newsitem.title: USA: ZDNet to offer free utility to manage Web "cookies".
newsitem.headline: ZDNet to offer free utility to manage Web "cookies".

text.p: Ziff-Davis Publishing's ZD-Net online unit Friday unveiled free software that enables computer users to determine which sites on the Internet can monitor their Web surfing in what the company said was a boost for consumers' privacy.

The software, dubbed Cookie Master, is designed to enable individuals to find out which monitoring programmes, known as cookies, have been downloaded onto their computer's hard drive and selectively delete unwanted ones.

Cookies are often automatically installed on hard disks when a person registers for a Web site, and in many cases they can be used to save time and help individuals gain access swiftly to relevant information.
But the use of cookies has been a hot issue this year. Privacy advocates have argued they can be intrusive and are often downloaded without a user's knowledge or approval.
"Cookie Master effectively takes the mystery out of Web cookies and puts privacy control back into the hands of Web users," said ZD-Net Executive Editor Preston Gralla.

Programmes such as Cookie Master can help put power back into users' hands and ease fears about communicating and carrying out transactions online, said Lori Fina, executive director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, a cyberspace-oriented free speech and privacy advocacy group.

Cookie Master, which requires the Windows 95 operating system, is available for free at the ZDNet Software Library on the Web (http://www.hotfiles.com). The programme provides users with a list of the cookies that reside on their hard drives and lets them see which Web sites installed them.
Individuals can also see what data has been stored in the cookies and delete any cookies they don't want.
Cambridge, Mass.-based ZD-Net is owned by Ziff-Davis Publishing, a unit of Softbank Corp.
